PG. Procter & Gamble.

His accounts have made multiple trades in the stock. Some reporting points to significant overall volume, potentially reaching into the millions across all the activity.

P&G makes the household brands that are in everyone's cupboard, and it runs enormous global manufacturing and supply chains to do it.

A large portion of its costs sit in imported materials, packaging, and components.

Which puts it directly in the path of the tariff agenda.

Higher import costs, reshoring incentives, and anything that moves consumer spending or industrial production feeds straight into how a company like this performs.
